bug_semantics: LiquidJS documents RenderOptions.ownPropertyOnly as a per-render lockdown that hides prototype-chain properties for a single parseAndRender()/render() call. Context stores the resolved flag as this.ownPropertyOnly = renderOptions.ownPropertyOnly ?? opts.ownPropertyOnly, and property reads go through readJSProperty(..., this.ownPropertyOnly). The {% render %} tag does not reuse the parent Context: it builds an isolated child via Context.spawn() (before July 2024, via an equivalent inline new Context({}, ctx.opts, {sync, globals, strictVariables})). That child RenderOptions object omits ownPropertyOnly, so the child falls back to the instance-level opts.ownPropertyOnly. A developer who keeps ownPropertyOnly:false on the Liquid instance for compatibility and then locks down an untrusted render with parseAndRender(..., { ownPropertyOnly: true }) is protected at the top level but still leaks prototype properties from any {% render %} partial. {% include %} is not this sink: it pushes onto the parent scope stack and keeps the parent's resolved flag.
flaw_origin: The incomplete child-context option copy already existed in {% render %} (6801552fe, 2021-12-11 copied only sync/globals/strictVariables). ownPropertyOnly was added as a documented RenderOptions field in 7e99efc51 (2022-01-29) but lookups still used this.opts.ownPropertyOnly, so a per-render override did not work anywhere. d48991623 (2023-02-14) first made the per-render override real by introducing Context.ownPropertyOnly and switching _getFromScope to this.ownPropertyOnly, without updating the {% render %} child constructor to pass the resolved flag. That is the first commit at which top-level parseAndRender(..., { ownPropertyOnly: true }) blocks prototype reads while {% render %} partials still re-derive the instance default. e443068cb (2024-07-09) later extracted the same incomplete RenderOptions object into Context.spawn() and switched render.ts to ctx.spawn(); that is a refactor of the already-vulnerable copy, not a first write.
